rationale: Reference class: short-window persistence of declared or de facto pauses in active interstate strikes; base rate about 0.85-0.90 per 3-day window (rough judgment, no fixed count). Resolution turns on US qualifying strikes on Iranian land, not on a formal ceasefire. Searches (Oct 30-31) found no ceasefire in force, an active war with Hormuz attacks, and mediation by Qatar and Pakistan; one aggregator reports Trump pledged no strikes before the Nov 3 midterms (single secondary source, unverified). Blockade enforcement at sea does not count. Kept near base rate; the main risk is a breakdown in mediation or a retaliatory strike.

Reference class: large private tech companies listing within about two weeks of a public S-1; base rate is near 0.02 without a public filing, but higher once one is on file. Anthropic publicly filed its S-1 on Oct 26, 2026 and applied for Nasdaq listing as ANT (SEC EDGAR and multiple trackers). No pricing date is confirmed. One tracker reports an S-1/A around Nov 5-10 and pricing/listing Nov 17-20, which falls after the Nov 15 deadline; this is unverified. Raised well above base rate on the public filing, but the reported timeline points past the deadline.

Reference class: decrees declaring a French état de siège under Article 36; essentially none in the modern Republic outside wartime or colonial crises, so base rate near 0.01. Searches found no 2026 decree. A new 'état d'alerte de sécurité nationale' regime (law of Aug 2026) and October 17-18, 2026 riots were reported, but neither is an état de siège, and the question excludes état d'urgence. Slightly above base rate for the riots.

Reference class: direct NATO-Russia kinetic incidents 2022-2026; the search found several NATO shootdowns of drones (Poland Sept 2025, Latvia June 2026, Lithuania Sept 2026) and frequent Romanian airspace violations, so incidents are not rare. Most appear to be drones of uncertain origin or one-way attack munitions aimed at Ukraine, which the criteria say do not alone qualify. A clearly qualifying Russian-forces engagement in about 2 weeks is less likely, so the estimate sits above a 0.05 base rate on incident frequency and the ambiguity of attribution.

Reference class: AAA titles with a firm date about 3 weeks out that are delayed again; base rate roughly 0.05. GTA VI has already slipped twice (May 2026 to Nov 19, 2026). Take-Two's CEO reaffirmed the Nov 19 date in earnings remarks, an SEC proxy statement, and interviews (search results, some dates inconsistent). Reaffirmation close to launch lowers the probability below base rate. Main risk: a late delay announcement, given the two prior slips.

Reference class: formal war declarations between great powers; none since 1945 (about 80 years), so base rate near 0.01 per window. The window closes about Nov 18, before GTA VI's Nov 19 date. The search found no declared or direct great-power war in 2026; risk assessments (CFR, US threat assessment) rate Russia-NATO and Taiwan crises as possible but not imminent. US-Iran fighting does not qualify because Iran is not a superpower. Slight allowance for resolver ambiguity.

Reference class: formal US announcements ending a naval blockade within about 3 months of imposition; base rate about 0.10 (rough judgment, few cases). The blockade was reinstated July 13-14, 2026 and is still in force as of Oct 28-31, with a maritime advisory covering all Iranian ports. Iran links Hormuz reopening to ending the blockade, and mediation (Qatar, Pakistan) is ongoing, which lifts the estimate a little. A qualifying announcement must be an unambiguous, official statement of a general end, and Trump has said only that the war will 'get wrapped up soon'. Partial exemptions do not count.
